//: Config for the job skill (~/.claude/skills/job). Read on every call by .claude/hooks/job-guard.mjs and by the job scripts. Keys starting with // are notes. Re-running /job init adds new keys and never changes your values.
//default_branch: The branch PRs go into. Pushing to it (and to main / master) is always reserved for the deployer.
//pr_tool: How jobs open PRs: gh | bitbucket-pr | none. Detected from the origin remote.
//role_env: The env var that carries a job's role into its tab: worker | deployer. Unset means the coordinator.
//reserved_commands: This project's deploy / release / merge commands. Only a deployer job, or the coordinator when the user asks, may run them. Each entry is {"pattern": <JS regex>, "what": <label>}. The hook anchors a pattern at a command position (after sudo / env / nohup / timeout / bash and VAR=x prefixes), so `grep "x deploy"` or an echo that mentions it still passes. {REST} stands for the rest of the same command, e.g. "aws\\b{REST}\\becs\\s+update-service\\b". Always reserved, without listing: pushing to the default branch, gh pr merge, glab mr merge, and PR-merge API calls.

reserved_commands.what: install the board plugin on this machine

//coordinator_commits: true lets the coordinator itself (not its subagents, not workers) edit files and run git commit / merge / pull / rebase here and in this repo's worktrees, inside Herdr, without a job or `here:`. For a repo the coordinator keeps itself, such as a home coordinator's ~/work. Read from the main checkout's job.json. Other job repos stay guarded by their own job.json. /job init never turns it on.
//worktree_links: Gitignored files and dirs that ~/.claude/skills/job/scripts/worktree-link-local.sh links from the main checkout into a job worktree, e.g. .env, node_modules, .venv. Paths are relative to the repo root.
//ports: Port bases for parallel jobs: label or env var name -> base. Job N gets base+N for every entry, with the first N >= 1 where all are free. Example: {"dev": 3100, "PLAYWRIGHT_PORT": 3200}.
//heavy_commands: Commands that load the machine (full builds, the full test suite, browser tests). Briefs tell workers to run them through ~/.claude/skills/job/scripts/with-heavy-lock.sh, one at a time per repo.
//max_active_jobs: How many of this repo's jobs may run at once: job agents working in its checkouts, in any Herdr workspace, whose job has no final report yet. Raise it on a bigger machine.
//max_dev_servers: How many jobs may run a dev server (on their `ports`) at once. At the limit, a job that needs one waits, or goes without; its brief says which.
//min_free_mb: Don't start a job, or a dev server, while the machine has less memory available than this, in MB (Linux MemAvailable; macOS free + inactive pages). Close finished job tabs first. ~/.claude/skills/job/scripts/mem-check.mjs checks it.
//ship_routine: What a build job does before its commit, pasted into every brief: free text, or a path to the doc that defines it (changelog, PR rules; the build number only without build_stamp, since with it the merge sets the number and PRs never bump it). Empty = commit, push and open a PR with pr_tool.
ship_routine: Commit, push and open a PR with gh (title and body per ~/ai-config/docs/pr-writing.md). Tests: S=$(mktemp -d); HOME=$S/home XDG_STATE_HOME=$S/state TMPDIR=$S/tmp JOB_BOARD_HOME=$S/board node --test (tests/guard.mjs refuses the real HOME). Never run board.mjs, the plugin or any test against the live board: no real HOME, XDG_STATE_HOME, JOB_BOARD_HOME or TMPDIR, cwd only inside scratch copies, no `herdr plugin action invoke` in the user's panes. Never restore or migrate live board files yourself: report it. No deploy and no plugin install: the board is installed after the merge.
//ship: Optional. How ~/.claude/skills/job/scripts/ship.mjs merges, releases, deploys and verifies this repo, written from its own runbook. Without it ship.mjs uses a built-in preset by folder name (release-notes-manager, sfc-integration, ai-config, herdr-job-board), else merges only (gh or bb-merge by pr_tool). Keys, each overriding the preset's: preset (a preset's name), merge (gh | bb-merge), aws ({VAR: value}; {repo} is the main checkout), release (targets that need a release PR first), default_targets, targets ({name: {deploy: [step], verify: [step]}}), install, verify_install. A step is {"cmd": [..], "cwd": "worktree" | "repo", "what": label} or a check: {"check": "http", "url"} | {"check": "ecs-rollout", "cluster", "service"}. ship.mjs <repo> <card> plan prints the result.
//build_stamp: Off unless you add a build_stamp key. With it, PRs never touch the build number or the changelog: each adds one fragment <fragments>/<branch-with-dashes>.md ("### Fixed" then "- **Title** (build {build}, date): …"), and ~/.claude/skills/job/scripts/bb-merge.mjs <repo> <PR> merges the PR, then writes ONE commit on default_branch through the Bitbucket API: the number in `file` + 1 (the line matching `line`, capture group = the number), every fragment folded under `section` in `changelog`, the fragments deleted. It refuses a PR that changes that line or the changelog, except a branch starting with `release_branches` that only renames the section heading to "## [X.Y.Z] - date". A PR without a fragment gets a warning, or is refused with require_fragment. Only file is required; the rest default to this example: {"file": "src/lib/build-version.ts", "line": "^export const APP_BUILD = (\\d+);", "changelog": "CHANGELOG.md", "section": "## [Unreleased]", "fragments": "changelog.d", "placeholder": "{build}", "release_branches": "release/", "require_fragment": false}
